Official final gamebook reports Green Bay 31, Chicago 7; complete lineups, substitutions, DNPs and inactives; Tyson Bagent starting for inactive Caleb Williams with Case Keenum later participating; and printed injury statuses for Skyy Moore, T.J. Edwards, Dayo Odeyingbo, Tyrique Stevenson and Benjamin St-Juste. Return-questionable and return-doubtful wording is not treated as an actual return.
Official Packers game center independently reports FINAL, Chicago 7 and Green Bay 31, and links the final gamebook.

Official final injury report binds injury-driven pregame statuses: CHI Caleb Williams questionable, Kyle Monangai and Keyshaun Elliott out; GB Aaron Banks and Jacob Monk doubtful, Chris Brooks and Savion Williams out, and Anthony Campbell and Javon Hargrave questionable. It also records active/no-game-status closures for the listed Bears and Packers participants.

Official final inactives list CHI Caleb Williams, Kyle Monangai, Keyshaun Elliott, Jamree Kromah, Ozzy Trapilo and Jayden Loving; and GB Jacob Monk, Aaron Banks, Donovan Jennings and Anthony Campbell. Kevin Zeitler was active.

Official club recap reports Javon Hargrave was carted off just after the fourth-quarter two-minute warning with an apparent Achilles injury, and confirms Skyy Moore left with an ankle injury and Benjamin St-Juste with a hamstring injury. It also reports Tyson Bagent was replaced by Case Keenum in the fourth quarter rather than documenting an injury-driven relief change.

Official Packers depth chart identifies the current source-bound position groups and primary depth candidates for Moore's receiver/return duties, Hargrave's defensive-tackle duty and St-Juste's cornerback duty. It is role evidence only and does not prove the Week 5 added-duty allocation by itself.

EA SPORTS' official Madden NFL 27 Week 4 player page identifies Anthony Campbell, player ID 4801, as a Green Bay Packers defensive tackle with OVR 64. The frozen non-QB calibration maps that OVR to 0.0 Walters points.

The official final gamebook lists Laken Tomlinson as Green Bay's starting left guard and Travis Glover as the starting right guard, records Jager Burton as Did Not Play, and lists Aaron Banks, Jacob Monk and Anthony Campbell among Green Bay's inactives. The same gamebook supplies the final 31-7 result and final participation record.

Green Bay's official postgame recap says Laken Tomlinson started at left guard for the second consecutive game, directly binding him as Aaron Banks' game-active primary replacement rather than inferring an anonymous committee.
EA SPORTS' official Madden NFL 27 Week 4 player page identifies Laken Tomlinson as Green Bay's left guard with OVR 74. The frozen non-QB calibration maps OVR 74 to 0.2 Walters points.
The NFL's official player log records Jager Burton with zero games and zero starts in Week 5, consistent with the official gamebook's DNP entry.

Chicago's official depth chart identifies Jack Sanborn as an active reserve linebacker, Daniel Hardy directly behind Dayo Odeyingbo, Clark Phillips behind Tyrique Stevenson and Josh Blackwell as the other active reserve boundary corner. The final gamebook records Phillips DNP and Sanborn, Hardy and Blackwell as substitutes, supporting labelled documented-depth estimates for only the vacated additional duties.

Green Bay's official final game updates confirm Bagent started for the injured Caleb Williams, Keenum entered in the fourth quarter, Moore left injured, and the documented Melton/Golden receiving and return work occurred after Moore's departure.

The official postgame recap describes Keenum replacing Bagent in the fourth quarter as a performance change rather than a second injury-driven quarterback loss, and confirms Hargrave's late injury departure.

NFL.com reports Tyson Bagent would start because Caleb Williams was injured and Case Keenum would be the second quarterback, binding Bagent as the primary injury replacement without relabelling the later performance benching.

The final gamebook confirms the 31-7 final and Week 5 activation/role check. Chicago starters include Kalif Raymond, Theo Benedet and Xavier Woods; Neville Gallimore is a participating substitute. Green Bay starters include Barryn Sorrell and Anthony Belton; Skyy Moore is a participating substitute before his return-questionable/out sequence, and Bo Melton and Matthew Golden perform receiving/return duties afterward.

Chicago's official transaction chronology confirms no pre-kickoff activation for the continued reserve cases. Noah Sewell's Oct. 10 activation is preserved separately; Shemar Turner's activation occurred Oct. 13 after the game.
Green Bay's official transaction chronology confirms no pre-kickoff activation for Zach Bako-Bewele, Jayden Reed, Micah Parsons or the other continued reserve cases.
The official biography binds Zach Bako-Bewele to the unchanged frozen Zach Tom identity, EA ID 22434. The existing 87 OVR and 1.2-point value are retained; no new calibration is created.

Chicago's official transaction log records the reserve placements relevant at the Oct. 11 kickoff: Jonathan Garvin on Aug. 4; Dallis Flowers on Aug. 7; Nephi Sewell on Aug. 25; Kyler Gordon, Noah Sewell and Shemar Turner on PUP and Brittain Brown, Tony Fields II, Jaylon Jones and Ray-Ray McCloud III on Reserve/Injured on Aug. 30; Coby Bryant and Hayden Large on Sept. 1; Braxton Jones on Oct. 3. It records Noah Sewell's Oct. 10 activation and Shemar Turner's later Oct. 13 activation. No pre-kickoff activation is recorded for the other named cases.

Chicago officially activated Noah Sewell from Reserve/PUP on Oct. 10, elevated Zavier Scott for the game, and downgraded Kyler Gordon and Shemar Turner to out. The final gamebook records Sewell and Scott as participants, so neither is treated as a reserve-list absence.

Green Bay's official transaction log records Collin Oliver and Savion Williams on IR/designated for return and Luke Musgrave, Micah Parsons and Jordon Riley on PUP on Aug. 30; Zach Bako-Bewele on IR Sept. 28; Jayden Reed on IR Sept. 30; Warren Brinson on IR Oct. 3; Edgerrin Cooper on IR Oct. 6; and Chris Brooks on IR Oct. 10. No pre-kickoff activation is recorded for those cases.

Green Bay's Aug. 30 roster announcement independently binds Oliver and Savion Williams to IR/designated for return and Musgrave, Parsons and Riley to PUP. A designation to return is not an activation or an actual return.

The Daily Gopher reports St-Juste played 10 special-teams snaps against Chicago and records no defensive statistic. This is useful role evidence but conflicts with the six special-teams snaps reported by Yahoo Sports and does not bind the exact injury play or added-duty successor.

Yahoo Sports reports St-Juste was limited to six special-teams snaps and identifies the other Packers cornerbacks' defensive snap totals. The special-teams total conflicts with the Daily Gopher report, so neither total is promoted as exact source-bound exposure.

The official final gamebook confirms Green Bay's 31-7 final, Kyler Gordon inactive, and Malik Muhammad, Cam Lewis and Tyrique Stevenson as active Chicago participants. It preserves Stevenson's no-return injury sequence and does not establish an actual Benjamin St-Juste return.

Week 5 snap reporting records Malik Muhammad at 49 defensive snaps, Cam Lewis at 36 and Tyrique Stevenson at 31. It explicitly reports that after Stevenson's injury Muhammad moved outside and Lewis moved into the slot. The counts establish role identity only; they are not used as workload weights.

The final gamebook identifies St-Juste as an active substitute and records only that his return was questionable after Q3 1:58. It does not record an actual return, exact injury play, special-teams snap total or successor duty.
The October 15 report states that St-Juste played ten special-teams snaps against Chicago and no defensive snaps or recorded statistic.

The current Packers weekly snap table lists St-Juste with ten Week 5 special-teams snaps (42 percent) and explicitly attributes its snap-count data to Pro Football Reference via nflverse. This independently matches the Daily Gopher total. The page also makes clear that it is a derived snap table, not official NFL play-participation evidence.

The roster analysis treats St-Juste as a special-teams ace and says J. Michael Sturdivant could replace those special-teams contributions if St-Juste were unavailable. It is prospective role evidence, not proof that Sturdivant assumed the Week 5 injury-created duty.
